A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 21-page versions of the same Electrostatic Field Matching paper, including Appendices A–D. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the prose, equations, figures, and table.

before.justification: v2 reports original EFM experiments on toy distributions, colored-MNIST translation and generation, and CIFAR-10 generation in Section 4, with additional empirical illustrations in Appendices C and D.

after.justification: v3 retains the original toy-distribution and image experiments in Section 4, together with the sensitivity analyses and comparator outputs in Appendices C and D.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same electrostatic construction, normalized-field regression objective, training-point sampling, and practical forward-only ODE inference. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions cover Gaussian-to-Swiss-roll transport, the Gaussian-to-two-Gaussians appendix example, colored-MNIST translation and generation, and CIFAR-10 generation. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Flow Matching in Figure 10, PFGM in Figures 11–12, and Cycle-GAN, DDIB, and DSBM in Appendix D's Figure 23.

E3.justification: The experimental settings in Section 4 and Appendix D are identical, including plate separations, batch sizes, optimization settings, Euler inference for toy experiments, and RK45 settings for images. Table 1 is unchanged.

E4.justification: The interplate-distance analyses in Figures 6, 8, and 19, boundary-crossing example in Figure 20, and training-volume comparison in Figure 22 are retained without revision. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The empirical illustrations retain the same qualitative reporting practice.

E6.justification: The sample grids, transport trajectories, and qualitative findings in Section 4 and Appendices C–D are identical, including poorer recovery at large interplate distances. No result entries or reported outcomes change.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, stochastic transport construction, compact-support assumptions, Theorem 3.1, and all lemmas and proofs in Appendices A–B are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same claims: an electrostatic paradigm for generation and distribution transfer, theoretical justification, and proof-of-concept experiments. The added code-access sentence does not alter these scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain the same interpretations and limitations concerning dimensionality, interplate distance, training volume, backward-oriented trajectories, and stopping at the first target-plane intersection.

D1.justification: v3 adds a direct link to the authors' FieldMatching code repository in the abstract. v2 provided PFGM and comparator source links in Appendix D but lacked this project-code reference. All implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to diffusion models, bridge matching, Flow Matching, and PFGM are unchanged. The project-code link introduces no new prior-work comparison.

P1.justification: A code-availability sentence is appended to the abstract, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The remaining wording, terminology, headings, and section order are retained.

P2.justification: The longer abstract causes limited text reflow across columns and pages 1–2. Figures 1–23 and Table 1 retain their content and design; pages 3–21 render identically.

improvement.justification: The new project-code reference fills a small gap in v2's reproducibility documentation by identifying where readers can find the EFM implementation. The scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged. The PDFs establish this documentation benefit, but not the repository's contents or completeness.
